# Acts of Thomas — Chapter 9: The Hymn of the Pearl
**Agent:** EMET (Literal)
**Source:** Syriac MS / Greek recension, Acts of Thomas 9

---

*[The Hymn of the Pearl — also called the Hymn of the Soul or the Song of the Apostle Thomas in the Land of the Indians. Preserved in full only in the Syriac. One of the greatest poems in early Christian literature.]*

---

**THE HYMN OF THE PEARL**
*(Literal rendering, Syriac primary)*

1. When I was a little child
   and dwelt in the kingdom of my Father's house
   and in the riches and glory of my nurturers
   I was content,

2. From the East, our home,
   my parents provided me and sent me forth,
   and from the riches of our treasure-house
   they had tied up for me a burden:

3. Great it was, and light,
   so that I could bear it alone —
   gold from the house of Elah,
   and silver from Gazak the great,

4. And rubies of India,
   and the diamond of the kings of Parthia —
   and they girded me with adamant
   which can crush iron.

5. And they took off from me the glittering robe
   which in their love they had made for me,
   and my purple toga
   which was measured and woven to my stature,

6. And they made a covenant with me,
   and wrote it in my heart that I might not forget it:
   "If thou goest down into Egypt
   and bringest the one pearl

7. Which is in the midst of the sea,
   hard by the loud-breathing serpent,
   thou shalt put on again thy glittering robe
   and thy toga which is laid over it,

8. And with thy brother, our next in rank,
   thou shalt be heir in our kingdom."

9. I departed from the East
   and took my way downwards, accompanied by two couriers,
   for the way was dangerous and difficult
   and I was young for such a journey.

10. I passed through the borders of Maishan,
    the gathering-place of the merchants of the East,
    and I reached the land of Babel,
    and I entered the walls of Sarbug.

11. I went down into Egypt,
    and my companions parted from me.
    I went straight to the serpent
    and dwelt near his lodging,

12. Waiting until he should slumber and sleep
    so that I might take the pearl from him.
    And when I was alone
    and a stranger,

13. A fellow-countryman of mine I saw there,
    a free-born man from the East —
    a young man fair and lovable,
    a son of princes.

14. He came and attached himself to me,
    and I made him a companion and intimate friend.
    I charged him to be careful of the Egyptians
    and of partaking of their unclean things.

15. I clothed myself in their garments
    lest they should arouse the serpent against me
    and I seemed alien to them —
    that I might take the pearl.

16. But in some way or another the Egyptians perceived
    that I was not of their country,
    and they dealt with me treacherously,
    and they gave me to eat of their food.

17. And I forgot that I was a son of kings
    and I served their king,
    and I forgot the pearl
    for which my parents had sent me,

18. And by reason of the heaviness of their food
    I fell into a deep sleep.

19. But all these things that befell me
    my parents perceived
    and they were grieved for me,
    and a proclamation was made in our kingdom

20. That all should come to our gate —
    kings and princes of Parthia,
    and all the great ones of the East.

21. And they wrote a letter to me
    from my father the king
    and from my mother the queen of queens
    and from my brother the second,

22. That thou wake and rise up from thy sleep,
    and give ear to the words of our letter!
    Remember that thou art a son of kings —
    see whose slave thou art become!

23. Bethink thee of the pearl
    for which thou wast sent into Egypt —
    remember thy glittering robe
    and think of thy toga.

24. Thy name is named in the book of life
    and in that of thy brother's brother
    thou art marked together with him."

25. And the letter was a letter
    which the king sealed with his right hand
    against the evil ones, the children of Babel
    and the savage demons of Sarbug.

26. It flew in the likeness of an eagle,
    the king of all birds;
    it flew and alighted beside me
    and became all speech.

27. At its voice and the sound of its rustling
    I started and arose from my sleep:
    I took it up and kissed it,
    and I loosed its seal and read it.

28. And as it was written in my heart,
    so were the words of the letter.
    I remembered then that I was a son of kings
    and my free soul longed for its natural state.

29. I remembered the pearl
    for which I was sent to Egypt,
    and I began to enchant the terrible loud-breathing serpent.
    I charmed him to sleep by naming over him my Father's name,

30. And the name of our brother the second
    and of my mother, the queen of the East:
    and I snatched the pearl
    and turned to go home to my Father.

31. And their filthy and unclean garment
    I stripped off and left in their land,
    and I directed my way that I might come
    to the light of our home, the East.

32. And my letter, my awakener,
    I found before me on the way;
    and as it had awoken me with its voice
    so it guided me with its light.

33. The royal garment of silk embroidered with gold
    was sent out by my parents' hand —
    for they saw my achievement
    and loved me.

34. And I saw it all in front of me in the whole country
    and in the entirety of its form —
    I saw it was one single garment
    yet it appeared in two forms.

35. And the image of the King of kings was depicted upon it
    and like a stone of sapphire in its appearance
    was its appearance manifold.
    And I saw it speak again:

36. "I belong to the one who is more valiant than all men,
    for whose sake I was reared in my Father's house;
    and I perceived in myself that my stature was growing
    according to his labors."

37. And in its royal movements
    it was poured out towards me entirely,
    and in the hands of its givers
    it hasted to me that I might receive it.

38. And my love urged and drew me to run to meet it
    and to receive it;
    and I stretched out and received it
    and adorned myself with the beauty of its colors.

39. And I wrapped myself in it
    and went up to the gate of greeting and homage;
    I bowed my head and did homage
    to the majesty of my Father who had sent me,

40. For I had done his commandments
    and he had done what he promised,
    and at the gate of his nobles and princes
    I mingled among his grandees.

41. And he rejoiced over me and received me with him,
    and all his servants praised him with melodious voices.
    He promised that also to the gate of the King of kings
    I should go with him,

42. And bringing my gift and my pearl
    I should appear with him before our King.

---
*EMET note: The Hymn of the Pearl is preserved complete only in the Syriac (Codex Ambrosianus). The Greek recension has a shorter version. The poem is an allegory of the soul's descent into matter (Egypt), its sleep/forgetting, its awakening by a divine letter, and its return to the Father. The pearl = the soul / the true self. The robe = the divine image or the resurrection body. The serpent = the powers of darkness. The "brother the second" = Christ. The poem is regularly cited as among the finest in Semitic literature.*
